tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on African and Caribbean Fusion Music

questions.question: Describe how african and caribbean fusion music are used in a piece of music you have studied. Use musical vocabulary.
questions.correctAnswer: A detailed description using precise musical vocabulary (e.g. specific terms from the AQA elements list), referencing a named piece with accurate observations about how the elements are used and their effect.

questions.question: Compare how two different pieces use african and caribbean fusion music. Explain the effect in each case.
questions.correctAnswer: A comparison of two pieces identifying similarities and differences in how african and caribbean fusion music are used, explaining the different effects created in each musical context, using comparative language.

questions.question: How could you use african and caribbean fusion music in your own composition or performance? Explain your choices.
questions.correctAnswer: A practical application showing understanding of how african and caribbean fusion music can be manipulated in composition or performance, with specific examples of choices made and their intended effect.

tests.name: Extended Practice
tests.description: Self-marked extended answers on African and Caribbean Fusion Music

questions.question: Full-Mark Response Compare the rhythmic features of an African drumming piece with a reggae track. Identify at least four rhythmic terms from the AQA list and explain their effect. <div class="
questions.correctAnswer: A grade 9 response will: identify polyrhythm and cross-rhythm; name Caribbean rhythmic devices (skank, one-drop, off-beat); explain cyclic structure; compare different fusion approaches; use precise AQA vocabulary from the elements list. Mark scheme: AO3 (analyse and evaluate) + AO4 (knowledge and understanding) = total marks for listening; AO1 (perform) + AO2 (compose) for coursework components
questions.explanation: Extended answer: aim for the mark-scheme points, in order, with the command word addressed.
